title: Aquastop Hose Fault
shortDescription: The aquastop safety hose has triggered or its sensor is faulty.
fullDescription: AEG dishwasher error E12 indicates aquastop hose triggered or sensor short. The control halts the wash program and displays the fault on the timer LEDs or digital display. Resolution depends on isolating the component and replacing as needed.

causes.cause: Aquastop hose triggered or sensor short

symptoms: E12 indicated by blinking lights or display
Door interlock may stay engaged briefly

fixSteps.title: Cancel and drain
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the program key for 3 seconds to cancel; the unit will attempt to drain.

fixSteps.title: Inspect filters and hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the bottom filter assembly, clean it, and check the drain hose for kinks.

fixSteps.title: Test component
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the dishwasher out, remove the kick panel, and test the suspected part with a multimeter against the AEG tech sheet.

whenToCallPro: For E12 caused by sealed components or PCB failure, contact AEG authorized service. Built-in dishwasher removal requires shutting off plumbing and electrical safely.

faq.a: On the inside of the door, on the right edge near the latch.

faq.q: Why is my AEG dishwasher beeping continuously?
faq.a: Active error codes trigger continuous tones until acknowledged. Press cancel to silence.

faq.q: Where is the AEG service plate?
faq.a: On the inside of the door, on the right edge near the latch.

title: Heater Element Open Circuit
shortDescription: The heating element circuit reads open.
fullDescription: AEG dishwasher error E52 indicates flow heater element failure. The control halts the wash program and displays the fault on the timer LEDs or digital display. Resolution depends on isolating the component and replacing as needed.
symptoms: E52 indicated by blinking lights or display
Door interlock may stay engaged briefly

fixSteps.title: Cancel and drain
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the program key for 3 seconds to cancel; the unit will attempt to drain.

fixSteps.title: Inspect filters and hoses
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the bottom filter assembly, clean it, and check the drain hose for kinks.

fixSteps.title: Test component
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the dishwasher out, remove the kick panel, and test the suspected part with a multimeter against the AEG tech sheet.

whenToCallPro: For E52 caused by sealed components or PCB failure, contact AEG authorized service. Built-in dishwasher removal requires shutting off plumbing and electrical safely.

faq.q: Why is my AEG dishwasher beeping continuously?
faq.a: Active error codes trigger continuous tones until acknowledged. Press cancel to silence.

faq.q: Where is the AEG service plate?
faq.a: On the inside of the door, on the right edge near the latch.

title: Pressure Sensor Calibration Lost
shortDescription: Pressure sensor calibration values are out of tolerance.
fullDescription: E32 indicates the analog pressure sensor is reading values that fall outside the calibrated empty-fill window stored in the EEPROM.

causes.cause: Air trap clogged with detergent residue

fixSteps.title: Clean air trap
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the lower spray arm, lift the filter and rinse the air trap chamber.

fixSteps.title: Inspect air hose
fixSteps.instruction: Trace the small clear hose from the trap to the pressure sensor; replace if cracked.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning fails, replace the sensor and let the dishwasher self-calibrate over the next cycle.

faq.a: No — fill is blocked until E32 clears.

title: Drain Pump Over-Current
shortDescription: Drain pump current exceeded threshold.
fullDescription: E34 logs when the drain pump draws more current than expected, typically due to a foreign object in the impeller.

fixSteps.title: Clean pump cavity
fixSteps.instruction: Open the drain pump access at the base and remove debris.

whenToCallPro: If pump bearings are worn, replace with the AEG service kit.

faq.q: Can I bypass the drain manually?
faq.a: Yes — remove the lower hose to drain into a shallow pan before service.

title: Heating Element Open
shortDescription: Wash heating element shows open circuit.
fullDescription: E35 indicates the wash heater is not drawing current. Wash temperature cannot be reached and cycle results are poor.

fixSteps.title: Test heater continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the kick plate and measure resistance across the heater terminals — expect 25 ohms.

whenToCallPro: Heater replacement on AEG dishwashers requires partial tip-back; call service if uncomfortable.

faq.a: Some quick-cold cycles still complete, but quality is reduced.

title: NTC Sensor Drift
shortDescription: Wash water temperature sensor reads outside calibration.
fullDescription: E36 fires when the NTC thermistor returns values that do not align with secondary measurements during the wash phase.

fixSteps.title: Run a hot vinegar cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Place a cup of vinegar on the top rack and run the longest hot wash to descale.

whenToCallPro: If E36 returns after descaling, replace the NTC.

faq.a: Often yes — heavy scale insulates the probe and biases readings.

title: Diverter Motor Position Lost
shortDescription: Spray arm diverter motor lost position feedback.
fullDescription: E37 trips when the diverter motor cannot find its home position, preventing spray arm switching.

fixSteps.title: Clean spray arm sump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the lower spray arm and rinse the diverter housing.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning does not clear E37, the diverter motor needs replacement.

faq.a: Lower rack cleans, upper rack underperforms until repaired.

title: Anti-Flood Float Activated
shortDescription: The anti-flood float in the base pan tripped.
fullDescription: E38 indicates water has accumulated in the anti-flood pan beneath the dishwasher, triggering the float and shutting off the cycle.

fixSteps.title: Inspect base pan
fixSteps.instruction: Tilt the dishwasher and check the base pan for water; identify the source.

whenToCallPro: Tub leaks usually require replacement; call AEG service for assessment.

faq.a: Remove the standing water under the unit and the float drops automatically.

title: Door Hinge Spring Tension Loss
shortDescription: Door does not stay open at intermediate angles.
fullDescription: E39 is detected when the door open-angle sensor reports the door dropping unexpectedly during loading.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hinge cords
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the lower side panels and check the hinge cord routing; replace if frayed.

whenToCallPro: Spring kits are inexpensive but installation requires careful tensioning — request service if uncertain.

faq.a: Yes, but loading is awkward and the door can slam.

title: AirDry Vent Motor Stalled
shortDescription: AirDry vent motor failed to open during dry phase.
fullDescription: E48 is logged on AirDry-equipped models when the venting motor does not reach its open position.

causes.cause: Vent door blocked by detergent residue

fixSteps.title: Clean vent door
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the upper-left vent flap with a damp cloth.

whenToCallPro: If the motor is stripped, replacement is straightforward but use AEG OEM parts.

faq.a: They will dry slowly; AirDry just speeds the process by venting humid air.

title: Dispenser Door Wax Motor Stuck
shortDescription: Detergent dispenser wax motor did not actuate.
fullDescription: E58 trips when the wax motor that releases the detergent door does not reach its open position within 60 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Clean dispenser cup
fixSteps.instruction: Scrub residue from the dispenser tray with hot water.

whenToCallPro: Wax motor replacement requires removing the inner door panel — call service if unfamiliar.

faq.a: Use AEG-recommended tablets to reduce gumming and prolong wax motor life.

title: Bluetooth Module Init Failure
shortDescription: Built-in Bluetooth module failed to initialize.
fullDescription: E68 indicates the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth module did not respond to the main board on power-up.

fixSteps.title: Reset network
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the connectivity button for 10 seconds to reset Wi-Fi/BT.

whenToCallPro: If reset fails, the module must be replaced by AEG service.

faq.a: No — only smart features are limited; cycles run normally.
